name: Price
summary: Price with an optional old price (sale), a text before and after it, and a VAT text. Amounts are formatted with Intl: en-US and euro by default, or the locale of the LocaleProvider.
use: Everywhere a product amount is shown.
avoid: Totals in an overview: use Cart summary.
anatomy: Old price (struck through, for a sale).
figmaProps: True: amount in the error color, old price visible.
Show compare, Show prefix, Show suffix, Show VAT
reactProps: Only shown when it is higher than amount.
Small text before and after the amount: "From", "per piece".
Fixed number of decimals, for example 3 for a unit price such as €0.523. Default: what the currency uses.
Shows the VAT text after the price. Default: nothing.
The hidden "Was" and "Now" for screen readers and the VAT texts. Defaults in DEFAULT_PRICE_LABELS.
behaviour: You can also use formatMoney(amount, currency, locale, decimals) on its own.
With decimals the amount always has that many decimals: 0.52 with decimals 3 is €0.520. In a list the decimal marks then line up.
The old price uses the same number of decimals as the amount.
a11y: Screen readers hear "Was €99.95 Now €79.95". A strike-through alone is not enough.
Prefix, amount, suffix and VAT text are read as one phrase, in that order: "From €0.523 per piece excl. VAT".
content: Show the VAT text when it is not clear from the page: "incl." for consumers, "excl." for business customers.
Use vat for the VAT text and suffix for the unit ("per piece", "per month"). Then the VAT text is the same everywhere and follows the language.
do: Use the same size and the same number of decimals for all prices in an overview.
dont: An old price that was never real.
open: Assumption: decimals is a fixed number, not a maximum. Change this if price lists show 0.52 and 0.523 next to each other.
Assumption: no VAT text by default. A shop chooses excl. or incl. itself; there is no global setting for it yet.
Rounding is left to Intl (half away from zero). There is no own rounding rule.
